The loss of the transcription factor FLI1 leads to Paris-Trousseau syndrome and thrombocytopenia due to impaired hematopoiesis and megakaryocyte differentiation.[10][11]
In addition to thrombocytopenia, all patients with Jacobsen syndrome have Paris-Trousseau syndrome, characterized by dysfunctional platelets with giant alpha granules.

Patients with Jacobsen syndrome may also have immunodeficiency, increasing their risk of ear and sinus infections, abnormal lymphocyte development, hypogammaglobulinemia, and poor response to vaccinations.[13][14]
